title: Frontend: Reverse Words in a String
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Reverse Words in a String. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(text). Reverse the order of whitespace-delimited words, preserving letters inside words and normalizing separators to one space. Blank text returns empty.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Trim the input, split on runs of whitespace, reverse the token sequence, and join with one space.
alternativeApproaches: Implement a separator-preserving variant and define precisely which separator attaches to which word after reversal.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Extra spaces; newline/tab; one word.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
